The City Series was the name of a series of baseball games played between the [Philadelphia Athletics](/wiki/Philadelphia_Athletics "Philadelphia Athletics") of the American League and the Phillies that ran from 1903 through 1955. After the A's move to Kansas City, Missouri in 1955, the City Series rivalry came to an end. The teams have since faced each other in [Interleague play](/wiki/Interleague_play "Interleague play") (since its introduction in 1997) but the rivalry has effectively died in the intervening years since the A's left Philadelphia. In 2014, when the A's faced the Phillies in inter-league play at [Oakland Coliseum](/wiki/RingCentral_Coliseum "RingCentral Coliseum"), the Athletics did not bother to mark the historical connection, going so far as to have a Connie Mack promotion the day before the series while the Texas Rangers were in Oakland.[[137]](#cite_note-137)

The first City Series was held in 1883 between the Phillies and the [American Association's Athletics](/wiki/Philadelphia_Athletics_(American_Association) "Philadelphia Athletics (American Association)").[[138]](#cite_note-138) When the Athletics first joined the American League, the two teams played each other in a spring and fall series. No City Series was held in 1901 and 1902 due to legal warring between the National and American Leagues.

Valine, like other branched-chain amino acids, is synthesized by bacteria and plants, but not by animals.[[9]](#cite_note-9) It is therefore an [essential amino acid](/wiki/Essential_amino_acid "Essential amino acid") in animals, and needs to be present in the diet. Adult humans require about 24 mg/kg body weight daily.[[10]](#cite_note-DRItext-10) It is synthesized in plants and bacteria via several steps starting from [pyruvic acid](/wiki/Pyruvic_acid "Pyruvic acid"). The initial part of the pathway also leads to [leucine](/wiki/Leucine "Leucine"). The intermediate [α-ketoisovalerate](/wiki/Alpha-Ketoisovaleric_acid "Alpha-Ketoisovaleric acid") undergoes [reductive amination](/wiki/Reductive_amination "Reductive amination") with [glutamate](/wiki/Glutamate "Glutamate"). Enzymes involved in this biosynthesis include:[[11]](#cite_note-11)

1. [Acetolactate synthase](/wiki/Acetolactate_synthase "Acetolactate synthase") (also known as acetohydroxy acid synthase)
2. [Acetohydroxy acid isomeroreductase](/wiki/Ketol-acid_reductoisomerase "Ketol-acid reductoisomerase")
3. [Dihydroxyacid dehydratase](/wiki/Dihydroxyacid_dehydratase "Dihydroxyacid dehydratase")
4. [Valine aminotransferase](/wiki/Valine%E2%80%94pyruvate_transaminase "Valine—pyruvate transaminase")

Like other branched-chain amino acids, the catabolism of valine starts with the removal of the amino group by [transamination](/wiki/Transamination "Transamination"), giving [alpha-ketoisovalerate](/wiki/Alpha-Ketoisovaleric_acid "Alpha-Ketoisovaleric acid"), an alpha-[keto acid](/wiki/Keto_acid "Keto acid"), which is converted to [isobutyryl-CoA](/wiki/Isobutyryl-CoA "Isobutyryl-CoA") through [oxidative decarboxylation](/wiki/Oxidative_decarboxylation "Oxidative decarboxylation") by the [branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex](/wiki/Branched-chain_alpha-keto_acid_dehydrogenase_complex "Branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex").[[12]](#cite_note-:0-12) This is further oxidised and rearranged to [succinyl-CoA](/wiki/Succinyl-CoA "Succinyl-CoA"), which can enter the [citric acid cycle](/wiki/Citric_acid_cycle "Citric acid cycle")

Busan is located on the southeastern tip of the [Korean Peninsula](/wiki/Korean_Peninsula "Korean Peninsula"). It is located on the coast, which determined the development of the whole city itself. The distance from Busan to [Seoul](/wiki/Seoul "Seoul") is about 314 km (195 mi). Busan borders low mountains to the north and west, and the [Korea Strait](/wiki/Korea_Strait "Korea Strait") to the south and east. The Nakdong River Delta is located on the west side of the city, and [Geumjeongsan](/wiki/Geumjeongsan "Geumjeongsan"), the highest mountain in the city, is on the north. The [Nakdong River](/wiki/Nakdong_River "Nakdong River"), South Korea's longest river, flows through the west and empties into the [Korea Strait](/wiki/Korea_Strait "Korea Strait"). The southeastern region, called [Yeongnam](/wiki/Yeongnam "Yeongnam") in Korea, encompasses both [Gyeongsang Provinces](/wiki/Gyeongsang_Province "Gyeongsang Province") and 3 metropolitan cities of Busan, [Daegu](/wiki/Daegu "Daegu") and [Ulsan](/wiki/Ulsan "Ulsan"). Ulsan lies northeast of Busan. The combined population exceeds 13 million.

The closest overseas area to Busan is [Tsushima](/wiki/Tsushima_Island "Tsushima Island"), [Japan](/wiki/Japan "Japan"), with a distance of about 49.5 km (30.8 mi). The closest Japanese mainland area to Busan is [Fukuoka](/wiki/Fukuoka "Fukuoka"), roughly 180 km (112 miles) away. Busan and Fukuoka are also sister cities.
